input.why: Take 2 has the clearest scene: she mistakes him for the Bureau, he breaks the news, and the two are plainly strangers. It also has the only fond line at the close. It needed a warmer middle and truer facts, so I lifted the bad-customer joke from take 1. Help's price and effect are per [0ea73f060cd8775217b8a2af].
changes: Replaced 'half' with 'part': the sheet says only a first instalment, part of the loan. Cut 'Forty small things', which turned the price into a joke she couldn't know.
Cut 'freshly stamped' and the 'opposite of the Bureau' line: neither did any work, and 'Your Bureau card' was there only to hold a fact. Merged her questions into one frightened line.
Lifted take 1's Bureau joke, sharpened it, and answered it with 'Part of him's gone home'. This is where she starts to like him, and it leads straight into the hint.
Rebuilt her refusal as a flinch: she asks, stops herself, then says not yet. His close now answers her and keeps the 'get some sleep' fondness and 'I'll bring the rest'.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: If you're from the Bureau, you're early. I'm still on shift.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: I'm not. I've just paid them part of your loan.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Who saw you? I don't know you. Who's been asking about me?

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Nobody saw. People say you're the kind one on the terrace.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Kind? The Bureau's my worst customer. Stays all day, never tips.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Part of him's gone home, then. We'll want one small thing.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: What thing? Don't tell me. I took it, but not yet.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Not yet, then. Get some sleep. I'll bring the rest.

learned: She took it; not ready yet.
